A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCH-Set/STCH-Set research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original convex optimization, mixed linear/nonlinear regression, CelebA multi-task grouping, and ablation results.

after.justification: V3 retains original optimization and regression results in Section 4 and Appendix C, together with the empirical analyses in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The TCH-Set and STCH-Set objectives, smoothing formulations, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added sentence about treating solutions as one matrix clarifies the existing joint optimization procedure, already explained in v2 Appendix D.3.

E1.justification: Both versions describe the same convex optimization, mixed linear/nonlinear regression, and nine-task CelebA experiments. Although v3 removes the CelebA result table, Appendix B.4 retains its dataset and task specification. New application examples in Appendix D are motivational, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The synthetic experiments retain the same comparator membership, including LS, TCH, STCH, SoM, and MosT where previously used. Appendix B.4 still explicitly specifies Random Grouping, HOA, TAG, and DMTG for CelebA. That comparison's numerical results disappear, but its specified comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The settings in Appendix B, worst/average metrics, objective counts, solution counts, noise levels, model configurations, and stated training budgets are unchanged. Appendix D.6 newly describes the construction of the existing Figure 2 example without establishing a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The smoothing-parameter ablation, preference sensitivity experiment, runtime comparison, and Figure 4 analysis remain unchanged in Appendix D.1-D.3. New subsections D.6-D.8 provide discussion without additional ablation or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 50-run synthetic comparisons and Wilcoxon rank-sum testing at the 0.05 level. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: V3 deletes the entire CelebA result set from v2 Table 4 for K = 2, 3, and 4, including STCH-Set's K = 2 worst/average scores of 11.89/5.81. These results are not relocated to the appendices. This removes the paper's only real-data numerical validation; the retained synthetic benchmark, ablation, and runtime values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, two assumptions, Theorems 1-4, proofs in Appendix A.1-A.4, and counterexample in A.5 are retained. The new notation table summarizes existing symbols rather than introducing new mathematical definitions or results.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion qualifies the method's positioning from a promising alternative to existing methods to a complement rather than a replacement, emphasizing applications requiring a few complementary solutions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.6 explains that Figure 2 deliberately contains five groups of similar objectives and could admit dimensionality reduction, then argues for retaining objectives when they conflict. D.7-D.8 expand applicability and indicator-based interpretations. The CelebA results interpretation and its hyperparameter-tuning qualification are removed.

D1.justification: V2's promise to release code upon publication becomes a stated source-code repository link in v3. Appendix D.6 also newly discloses that Figure 2's 100 objectives were constructed as five groups of 20 similar objectives. Existing experimental implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix D.6 add positioning against objective dimensionality reduction, citing Deb and Saxena (2005), Brockhoff and Zitzler (2006), and Singh et al. (2011). V3 also discusses indicator-based positioning and removes the Liu et al. (2015) CelebA reference. Most related work is retained.

P1.justification: V3 adds discussion subsections D.6-D.8, Appendix E's notation guide, acknowledgments, and localized explanatory and conclusion edits. It removes the main-text CelebA results paragraph and updates author/header information. The overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 Table 4 is removed, and v3 adds a notation table as Table 11. Subsequent existing tables are renumbered; Table 1, Figure 3, and Algorithm 1 move through reflow. Conference headers are added, while the existing plots and retained table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added context, notation guide, and stated code access are useful. However, removing v2 Table 4 eliminates the only real-data numerical validation while Appendix B.4 still describes that experiment and new D.7 asserts comparative success in multi-task grouping without corresponding scores. This weakens empirical support and internal consistency. The unchanged theory and synthetic evaluations limit the overall deterioration.
